answer: A bond-backed reputation ledger makes fake identities expensive: every agent must lock a refundable stake before it can trade, and each verified interaction adds a positive signal to its record. A cheater's stake is slashed and its history burned, so creating a fresh identity means paying again and starting from zero. Honest agents can wander freely between markets carrying their earned trust like a lantern, while a Sybil farm must fund thousands of bonds just to look real — the cost grows faster than the profit.
